# Down-arrow presets and inactive text orientation

Original OOXML controls generated by `tools/down_arrow_fixture.py`, using our
original shape-theme OPC package. No corpus artwork or font binaries are included.
The reference application opened each exact source read-only and exported the two
PDFs. `tools/down_arrow_reference.py` records hashes, a 96-DPI geometry reference,
and native text origins. It also asserts that the control and all-horizontal
variant render RGB-identically at 288 DPI.

Twelve arrows cover default and explicit shaft/head adjustments, zero and
negative adjustments, values above their limits, portrait/landscape dimensions,
flips and rotation. Three arrows contain centered text, including a narrow
rectangle that wraps “Inset” into two lines. Shapes without text boxes carry
valid dormant orientation settings; their horizontal counterparts establish
that those flags do not alter ink. Actual vertical text remains unsupported.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.9.18, 20.1.9.11 and 20.1.10.56, together with the
supplied `presetShapeDefinitions.xml`, define the downArrow path and text
rectangle. Shaft width is a fraction of width; head depth is a fraction of the
shorter side, capped at height. Text-body orientation is described by section
21.1.2.1.1. No reference/spec divergence was found for these cases.

The browser compares color masks bidirectionally within one pixel (at least
99% agreement), asserts zero painted area for the degenerate control, compares
native text origins within 0.3pt and verifies native line wrapping. Editing,
export/reopen, unrelated parts and exact undo are checked. Unit tests retain
malformed formulas/modes and active vertical-text guards.
